34.author: St. Cyril of Alexandria
34.work: Commentary on the Gospel of John, Book 12
34.text: Cyril reads the water and the blood that flowed from the side of the crucified Lord as the birth of the sacraments from the wound of love. The water is Baptism; the blood is the Eucharist. Where Eve was drawn from the side of the sleeping Adam, the Church is drawn from the side of the new Adam asleep on the cross. Cyril is careful not to soften the physical fact — these are real fluids from a real wound — but he insists that the Spirit who oversaw the creation of Eve was at work again here, fashioning a bride for the Son.

34.author: St. John of Damascus
34.work: Exact Exposition of the Orthodox Faith, Book IV
34.text: Three centuries after Cyril, John of Damascus gathers the patristic tradition into a single formula. The water from the side gives birth to us in Baptism; the blood feeds us in the Eucharist; both flow from the same crucified body of God. The Christian life is therefore framed at its beginning and sustained at its center by what came out of that single wound. The Cross is not only the place of atonement; it is the source of the Church's sacramental life.
